canonical_statement: Erdos problem 3 (erdosproblems.com/3, OPEN). Verbatim source statement: "If $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}=\infty$ then must $A$ contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions?" Formalized (Lean, verbatim): ∀ A : Set ℕ, (¬ Summable fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) → ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength k. The conclusion is Filter.Frequently at ∃ᶠ: for every N there exists some k ≥ N such that A contains an arithmetic progression of length k — i.e. AP lengths attained by A are unbounded (infinitely many lengths k are realized), NOT that every k is realized.

must_determine: a proof (construction, density argument, or transfer theorem) that divergent reciprocal sum forces unbounded attained AP lengths
verification that the AP predicate used matches the Lean library's Set.IsAPOfLength (no unstated d ≥ 1 or distinctness strengthening unless the library itself imposes it)
explicit handling of the ∃ᶠ quantifier: unboundedness of attained lengths, not merely infinitely many APs of one fixed length
close_branch_A.statement: AFFIRMATIVE: prove that for every A ⊆ ℕ with divergent reciprocal sum, the set of k for which A contains some S ⊆ A with S.IsAPOfLength k is unbounded in ℕ (equivalently ∃ᶠ k in atTop, per the Lean statement). This may be done either by a direct proof or by proving a stronger statement (e.g. all k, or positive-density transfer) — a stronger proof is acceptable since it entails the target.

must_determine: an explicit or existence-proof counterexample set A with divergent reciprocal sum
a proof that A's AP lengths are bounded (no IsAPOfLength-k subset for any k above the bound), matching the negation of Filter.Frequently
consistency of the construction with the library's IsAPOfLength conventions (difference-zero degenerate APs included or excluded exactly as the library decides)
close_branch_B.statement: NEGATIVE: construct (or prove existence of) a set A ⊆ ℕ with ∑_{n∈A} 1/n = ∞ whose attained AP lengths are bounded above — i.e. there is some K such that for all k > K, no S ⊆ A has S.IsAPOfLength k. This is the exact negation of ∃ᶠ; it suffices that only finitely many lengths k are attained (e.g. no APs longer than some fixed K0), which is weaker than missing one specific length while possibly containing longer APs.

definitions: A : Set ℕ, an arbitrary subset of the natural numbers
divergent reciprocal sum: the series fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ) is NOT Summable in ℝ (equivalently its partial sums over A diverge to +∞; all terms are positive so non-summability = divergence)

S ⊆ A and S.IsAPOfLength k: S is a set which is an arithmetic progression of length k, as defined by the Lean library predicate Set.IsAPOfLength used in the formalization; the contract defers to that library definition verbatim (including its conventions on the common difference d, degenerate/difference-zero cases, and whether S is given as the image of an order-embedding of Fin k). No strengthening (e.g. forcing d ≥ 1 or distinctness) may be assumed beyond what the library predicate states

∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, P k means: ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ k ≥ N, P k — i.e. P holds for infinitely many, arbitrarily large k. It does NOT mean P holds for every k, and containing a k-term AP need not imply containing a (k+1)-term AP
quantifier order: for ALL A ⊆ ℕ with divergent reciprocal sum, THERE must exist arbitrarily large k each admitting SOME S ⊆ A with S.IsAPOfLength k; the k and S may depend on A
the question is a yes/no decision: answer(sorry) ↔ the displayed universal statement; 'arbitrarily long' in the prose glosses ∃ᶠ (unbounded attained lengths), not ∀k
invariants_that_must_survive_every_refor: the hypothesis is exactly non-summability (divergence) of ∑_{n∈A} 1/n over A ⊆ ℕ — no density, sparseness, or growth condition may be added
the conclusion is ∃ᶠ k in atTop (unbounded attained AP lengths), exactly as in the Lean statement — never silently upgraded to ∀k nor downgraded to a single k
S ⊆ A: the progression's terms must all lie in A
S.IsAPOfLength k is the Lean library predicate, with its exact conventions on length, common difference, and degenerate cases
the universal quantifier over ALL A ⊆ ℕ with divergent reciprocal sum
A, S are sets of natural numbers (integrality of the underlying domain); the reciprocal sum is taken in ℝ
known_traps: misreading ∃ᶠ in Filter.atTop as 'for every k': the Lean conclusion requires only unboundedly many attained lengths; a proof of ∀k is stronger (still a valid close of A), but a claimed refutation missing one fixed k0 while containing longer APs does NOT negate ∃ᶠ
conversely, accepting 'A contains APs of infinitely many lengths below a bound' or 'APs of one fixed length' as a close of branch A — unboundedness over k is required

silently strengthening Set.IsAPOfLength to require common difference d ≥ 1 or distinct terms without checking the library definition; if the library permits d = 0, a degenerate-AP-based argument may be vacuous or a counterexample may fail

using Szemerédi's theorem directly: it applies to positive upper density sets; divergent reciprocal sum does NOT imply positive upper density (e.g. primes), so the transfer must be justified, not assumed
citing the known implication from the Erdős AP conjecture as if it settled the problem — it is a conditional reduction, a non-result
confusing ∑_{n∈A} 1/n divergence with ∑ 1/n over an interval or with the full harmonic series
constructing a counterexample whose reciprocal sum converges, or whose AP lengths are unbounded, and mislabeling it a branch-B close
non_results: proving 3-term or any fixed-length-k AP existence under divergent reciprocal sum, without unboundedness over k
results under a stronger hypothesis than divergent reciprocal sum (e.g. positive density, positive relative density in [N,2N] for all N) — these are conditional strengthenings, not closes
a reduction to the Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions or another open conjecture of comparable strength, without proving it
almost-all-A or measure/density-generic statements when the statement quantifies over ALL A with divergent sum
bounds on how long APs must be for 'typical' A, or lower bounds on the reciprocal sum needed for a fixed k
APs of lengths along a selected infinite subsequence presented as the full answer when the proof does not establish unboundedness of attained lengths for every divergent-sum A
heuristic or probabilistic constructions without a rigorous proof of divergence of the reciprocal sum AND boundedness of AP lengths
permitted_background: Szemerédi's theorem: every subset of ℕ with positive upper density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions

the Erdős–Turán / density-recursive-transfer machinery: the conjecture is known to follow from the Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions (∑_{n∈A} 1/n diverges for dense-enough A); standard reductions in the literature on Erdős problem 3 may be cited as context
elementary facts about harmonic sums and reciprocal sums of subsets of ℕ
known partial results: Bloom–Sisask and related results giving 3-term (and longer fixed-length) APs under large reciprocal-sum hypotheses
basic Lean/Mathlib semantics of Summable, Set.IsAPOfLength, and Filter.Frequently as used in the formalization
